title: Investment time horizon

objectives.text: Define an investment time horizon and identify your own.
Explain why the horizon should determine how much market risk you take.
Adjust a plan when a goal moves closer.

explanation: Your time horizon is when you will need the money. It is not when you start investing. A retirement corpus needed in 25 years and a school fee needed in 18 months are both investments, but they cannot carry the same risk. SEBI's investor guidance is to match the investment to the horizon: money needed soon belongs in safer, more accessible products.

The horizon matters because it decides how much time you have to recover from a fall. Share prices can be down for years at a stretch. If you need the money during that period, you may be forced to sell at a loss. If you have a long horizon, you can wait for a recovery, and compounding has more time to work. That is why long-term goals can carry more equity risk than short-term ones.

Horizons also change. A goal that was ten years away becomes two years away, and the plan should shift towards safety as the date approaches. Reviewing the horizon once a year, and moving money for near-term goals into deposits or liquid options, prevents a market fall from derailing a plan you cannot postpone.

examples.title: Same person, two horizons
examples.text: Priya is saving for a car in two years and for retirement in 25 years. The car money goes into a fixed deposit so it is available and stable. The retirement money can stay in a diversified equity portfolio, because a fall in year five still leaves two decades to recover.

examples.title: When the goal gets closer
examples.text: Rahul's daughter's college fees are due in three years. He has been investing monthly in an equity fund. As the date approaches, he moves each year's contribution into a fixed deposit, so a market fall in the final year cannot reduce the amount he has already secured.

keyTakeaways: The time horizon is when you need the money, not when you invest.
Short horizons need safer, accessible products; long horizons can carry more market risk.
A long horizon gives compounding time and room to recover from falls.
Shift towards safety as a goal approaches.

review.notes: Matching investments to the horizon and avoiding equity for short-term needs are checked against SEBI's risk-management page. Market-risk and volatility points are checked against SEBI's key-risks page. No specific asset-allocation percentages are given. Awaiting a named human reviewer.

quiz.question: What is an investment time horizon?
options: The date you opened the account
The length of the fund's name
The date when you will need the money
quiz.explanation: The horizon is the period until you need to use the money. That date, not the purchase date, decides how much risk the money can carry.

quiz.question: Why can a long horizon carry more market risk than a short one?
options: There is more time to recover from a fall and for compounding to work
Markets never fall over long periods
quiz.explanation: A long horizon gives the investment time to recover from temporary falls and lets compounding build the corpus. It does not remove risk entirely.

quiz.question: Your child's fee is due in two years and the money is in an equity fund. What is the sensible adjustment?
options: Increase equity risk to catch up
Move that money towards safer, accessible products as the date approaches
Ignore it until the fee is due
quiz.explanation: As the horizon shortens, there is less time to recover from a fall. Shifting near-term money to safer products protects the goal.

disclaimer: General financial education, not personalised advice. The right horizon and asset mix depend on your own goals and obligations.
